beats.say: Velcro's first design had no loops at all. Just hooks, grabbing other hooks.
Its inventor, George de Mestral, later said it began in nineteen forty-one: burrs in his dog's ears, and under a microscope, hooks like tiny chamois horns.
Ten years later he patented nylon hooks. Loop a thread over a hot bar, snip one side, and the loop becomes a hook.
But with hooks on both strips, his own later patent says, only about thirty percent of them caught.
So in nineteen fifty-seven he turned one side into soft loops. About a thousand in every square centimetre, and far more hooks find something to grab.
He called the invention five percent of the work. The rest was sweat. Hooks that missed, until they didn't.
